principles: Pre-registration before implementation: the protocol document must be committed and hash-referencable before any harness code exists.
Reuse over rebuild: the plan binds to the existing instrument and smoke coverage instead of inventing new instrumentation.
No-overclaim: every claim in the landed document carries its boundary (instrument-not-agent, enumerated-classes-only, environment-bound).
drivers: Operator approval on 2026-07-05 to start the campaign, with the explicit instruction to land a supporting document first.
The rev 2 self-review proved the draft needed hardening (21 findings, incl. a no-op tamper class that would have spuriously falsified H2) — landing the hardened rev 3 locks that state.
M0 needs a committed plan to freeze protocol.json against.

options.name: Docs-only story landing rev 3 now
pros: M0 can reference a commit hash
cons: one more story in the pipeline before code starts

options.name: Bundle the doc with the M0 implementation story
cons: protocol semantics and harness code reviewed together — a reviewer finding on the doc forces re-review of code; weakens pre-registration

options.name: Keep the doc uncommitted and start M0 from the draft
cons: violates the repo's committed-generator/pre-registration policy; the draft could drift after M0 freezes against it

rationale: Pre-registration discipline requires the reviewed protocol text to be immutable-by-commit before M0 freezes protocol.json against it; the marginal cost of one docs story is small and the review surface stays clean.

preMortem.scenario: Landed doc drifts from what M0 implements (spec-vs-code divergence)
preMortem.trigger: M0 makes fingerprint/viability decisions that contradict the doc without updating it
preMortem.consequence: protocol.json and the pre-registration disagree; reviewers cannot tell which is authoritative
preMortem.mitigation: M0's story cites the doc's commit hash; fingerprint/viability decisions are recorded IN protocol.json with the doc as semantic source; contradictions require a doc revision story

preMortem.scenario: Concurrent same-path draft collision with another host
preMortem.trigger: another host drafts at docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-evidence-instrument-replay-execution-plan.md while this story is in flight
preMortem.consequence: DONE merge conflict or silent overwrite of one draft
preMortem.mitigation: draft already removed from the main working tree into this worktree; single-path scope; scratchpad backup preserves our text; DONE merge fails loudly on collision

preMortem.scenario: Reviewers relitigate plan design and stall the docs story
preMortem.trigger: REVIEW lanes treat pre-story design decisions (already adversarially reviewed, 21 findings resolved) as new story findings
preMortem.consequence: docs story loops without improving the deliverable
preMortem.mitigation: story deliverable is defined as landing reviewed rev 3 verbatim-in-substance; only genuinely new blocking defects are fixed in-story with the revision note updated

preMortem.scenario: Section 11 full-profile cost assumption proves wrong at M0
preMortem.trigger: 1M-record generate+verify cycle costs far more than expected
preMortem.consequence: schedule/budget claims in the landed doc look wrong
preMortem.mitigation: the plan defers full-N and the budget cap to M0 calibration (recorded unknown); a bad cost number changes protocol.json parameters, not the landed doc's validity
